content:
Ben (eng-infra): heads up — I'm landing a Terraform change that wires per-model ConfigMaps via kustomize overlays. goal: allow model-specific runtime knobs (batch_size, max_tokens, quant_profile) without a full monolith config rollout. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/terraform/+/r1234

Ben (eng-infra): terraform will create a `kubernetes_manifest` for the ConfigMap and patch the Deployment template with an annotation `configmap-hash: {{file_sha256}}` so k8s does a rolling update. question: does runtime pick up the file update without restart, or do we rely on the rollout? any objections to using the annotation approach?

Alice M.: ping — important: runtime currently watches `config.json` for flag-level hot reloads, but per-model sections are read into memory at process start for perf. short: file change alone won't update running model workers reliably. we need either a rolling restart or a targeted signal to reload model config.

Carlos (eng-runtime): +1 to Alice. we implemented inotify for feature flags (global) but model-specific knobs live in an in-memory map keyed by model name. reloading safely requires: 1) update in-memory map with atomic swap, 2) ensure existing requests finish or use per-request config lookup. practically speaking, a rolling restart is the safest for now.

Ben (eng-infra): ok noted. plan A: keep the annotation so k8s triggers Deployment rolling update. Plan B: add a `kubectl rollout restart deploy/$D` as part of the TF apply pipeline if annotation isn't acceptable. which do people prefer?

Dana S.: don't put secrets in ConfigMaps — confirm: are any of these per-model values secret (api keys, signer tokens)? if so we must map to Secret + ExternalSecret, not ConfigMap. also watch ExternalSecrets sync delay — can cause mismatch if rollout happens before secret is present.

Ben (eng-infra): good call. none of the new keys are secrets — just numeric knobs and quant_profile string refs. secrets (KMS-backed) remain in `redwood-secrets` via external-secrets. i'll make sure Terraform keeps them separate.

Emily P.: i can review the PR later today. for rollout: propose canary 10% for 30m, track per-model latency and error-rate dashboards (console -> per-route). if anything spikes, auto rollback. who sets the canary? infra or runtime?

Carlos (eng-runtime): runtime can set per-model health gates. we have a simple canary controller that reads `canary-weight` annotation on the Deployment and adjusts traffic via the routing proxy. infra can set annotation, runtime will enforce rollback if metrics exceed threshold.

Ben (eng-infra): PR updated with example kustomize snippet in `overlays/model-xyz/kustomization.yaml`:
```yaml
resources:
  - ../../base
patchesStrategicMerge:
  - configmap-patch.yaml
commonAnnotations:
  configmap-hash: "sha256:abcdef..."
```
and terraform snippet (pseudo):
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_manifest" "model_xyz_cm" {
  manifest = yamldecode(file("./manifests/model_xyz_cm.yaml"))
}
# compute hash from file and set in deployment patch
```

Ben (eng-infra): also note: we compute the sha locally during `terraform plan` with a helper script so the plan shows the intended rollout.

Dana S.: sounds good. add a readiness probe that checks config schema parsing on startup so if we accidentally push malformed config the pod won't become ready. also add an alert for ExternalSecrets sync lag > 60s.

Emily P.: i'll add my review comments re: logging and metrics. @Ben can you include what dashboard panels to watch in the PR description?

Ben (eng-infra): will do. PR updated with dashboard links and a suggested canary playbook (10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 hours, rollback command included).

deploy-bot: terraform plan finished for r1234 — 2 changes to ConfigMap, 1 change to Deployment annotations. run `terraform apply` to proceed.

Ben (eng-infra): thanks. i'm going to run apply in the canary workspace this afternoon and watch the first model group. will post results here + any rollback. :thumbsup:
